clue.text: Weapon obtained from promising American girl

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman or girl
a girl who is promising is giving her word, so the American girl's promise is the ..., supplying the possessive S and WORD

explanation.surface: A weapon is handed over by an American girl full of promise.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a girl making a promise: a broad's word, run together, spells the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsword is a heavy sword with a wide blade, a classic cutting weapon.

clue.text: Deplorable Parisian traffic jam?

explanation.surface: A Paris gridlock described as something lamentable.
explanation.walkthrough: In Paris a street is a rue; a jammed street is a rue that is full, which is how the word sounds when split.
explanation.definitionFit: Rueful means regretful or pitiable, hence deplorable; the second reading jokes that a crowded French street is a full rue.

clue.text: Rat in a river, say

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
to state something is to say it

explanation.surface: A rodent is spotted swimming in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' looks like the animal, but here it means a turncoat; the Po is the crossword's favourite Italian river.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat is to desert a cause, and someone who abandons their faith or party is a renegade of that kind.

clue.text: Shrewd, in a way

explanation.surface: Someone is described as clever, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' looks like a hedge meaning 'somewhat'; read literally, it is wise in the manner of a street (way), streetwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Streetwise means savvy about urban life, so astute; the second reading takes 'way' as a road and '-wise' as 'in the manner of'.

clue.text: To make a choice, I act for the best

parts.note: to opt is to make a choice
to mum is an old word for performing in a mummers' play, so to act

explanation.surface: Someone chooses and acts with the best intentions.
explanation.walkthrough: MUM here is the verb from mummers, the folk players who acted mimed plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the most favourable condition or outcome, i.e. the best possible.

clue.text: Land's End astern? That's absurd

indicators.note: the end of the word Land's, its final letter before the possessive, is wanted

parts.note: astern on a ship means at the back, aft

explanation.surface: Moving the tip of Cornwall to the back of a boat would be ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the far tip of Cornwall in south-west England; here it just means the last letter of 'Land', D.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft is British informal for silly or foolish, so ridiculous.

clue.text: As a result of espionage, it will be blown up

definitions.text: As a result of espionage, it will be blown up

parts.words: As a result of espionage, it will be blown up
parts.note: sounds like a spy's bomb exploding, but the thing a spy produces is a tiny photograph that must be enlarged to be read

explanation.surface: A spy's handiwork is set to explode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown up' means enlarged, as a photograph is, not detonated.
explanation.definitionFit: A microdot is a photograph shrunk to the size of a full stop, used by spies to hide documents and magnified to be read.

clue.text: How old maid is moved in physical contact

explanation.surface: An elderly spinster being carried about by people grappling her.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Maid is a card game in which cards are passed from player to player; 'old maid' is not a woman here.
explanation.definitionFit: In the card game the cards pass from one player to the next; fighting at close quarters is body-to-body combat.

clue.text: Barbarian leader settled back at first

indicators.note: first says the word at is placed at the front of the answer
back means the word for settled is read in reverse order

parts.note: a bird that has settled has alit

explanation.surface: A barbarian chief is said to have settled back at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the word for settled round (giving TILA), and 'first' says the clue's 'at' leads the answer; 'Barbarian leader' is the definition, not a first-letter signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruler of the Huns in the fifth century was the archetypal barbarian chief who ravaged the Roman Empire.

clue.text: Political type held back by star comedian

indicators.note: held back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A politician is held up by a famous comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' reverses TARCOMED, found across 'star comedian', to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US party of that name, or any believer in popular government, is a political figure.

clue.text: Occupying queer street outside bull-ring

explanation.surface: Someone is living on a strange road around a bullfighting arena.
explanation.walkthrough: Queer Street is old British slang for being in debt. On an archery target the gold bull is ringed by red, so outside the bull you are in the red.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overdrawn is shown in red ink, so owing money is being in the red; on a target the ring round the bullseye is red.

clue.text: Enjoyment would be sure to follow this request

definitions.text: Enjoyment would be sure to follow this

explanation.surface: An appeal that is certain to bring delight.
explanation.walkthrough: Put SURE after this four-letter word and you get a word for enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest appeal; followed by 'sure' it makes a word meaning delight.

clue.text: Except for some Europeans, extremely different

explanation.surface: Things are very different if certain Europeans are left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apart from Poles' is a way of saying 'except for some Europeans'.
explanation.definitionFit: Things as far apart as the North and South ends of the earth are utterly unlike; read literally it means setting aside the people of Poland.

clue.text: Risky way to make brief contact

explanation.surface: A dangerous method for a fleeting meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: touch something and then leave at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A touch-and-go situation is precarious with an uncertain outcome; literally, touching and then going is a brief contact.

clue.text: Musical season — watch part

parts.note: Hair is the famous 1960s rock musical
spring is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: A musical's run for the season is something to keep an eye on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' is a timepiece, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine coiled spring that regulates the balance wheel in a mechanical timepiece.

clue.text: Lake and large peninsula in part of Africa

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps
Iberia is the large peninsula holding Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A geography lesson pairing a lake and a peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a West African republic founded for freed American slaves.

clue.text: Commonplace restriction, Italy ordered

parts.note: a ban is a restriction or prohibition

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of Italy are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A dull limit on Italy's affairs has been imposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' shuffles the country's name (giving ALITY) to follow the word for restriction; 'Commonplace' is a noun here, a platitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A commonplace, as a noun, is a trite remark, and triteness or a trite saying is a cliché of this kind.

clue.text: A unit I'm forming into a detail

indicators.note: forming says the letters of a unit I'm are shaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A soldier is reporting how a small unit became one tiny part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forming into' looks like military drill, but 'forming' rearranges A UNIT I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: A minutia is a small, trivial point, one particular among many.

clue.text: Lack of fair features in single reform in America

indicators.note: the second in places the rearranged letters within the abbreviation for America

parts.note: US is short for the United States, America

indicators.note: reform means the letters of single are re-made in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An American campaign for single people turns out unattractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges the clue's 'single' (giving GLINES), and the second 'in' sets that inside the abbreviation for America; 'fair' means good-looking, not just.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainness of appearance means an absence of good looks, 'fair' meaning beautiful.

clue.text: It may be binding on a novel state

definitions.text: It may be binding on a novel

explanation.surface: A rule that could be enforced in a newly formed country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binding' is a book's cover, not a legal obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is fine goatskin leather used for book covers, and also a North African kingdom.

clue.text: Peter won't be seen in one of these suits

definitions.text: Peter won't be seen in one of these suits

parts.words: Peter won't be seen in one of these suits
parts.note: reads like a man's clothes, but in bridge a peter is a high-then-low signal that needs at least two cards in a suit, impossible when a suit holds only one card

explanation.surface: A man called Peter refuses to wear certain outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suits' are card suits; in bridge, to peter is to signal by playing a high card then a low one in the same suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit holding just one card in a bridge hand is so called, and a lone card cannot make the two-card signal.

clue.text: Noble cricket groundsman

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who looks after a cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Lord founded and tended Lord's, the famous London cricket ground that bears his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a nobleman by title; Thomas of that surname was the eighteenth-century groundsman behind London's best-known cricket ground.

clue.text: Ignore reorganization in country department.

indicators.note: reorganization means the letters of Ignore are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat advises disregarding a shake-up in a rural office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country department' looks like a government office but means an area of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A district or area within a nation, like a French département.

clue.text: Italian architect's boy enters race in Siena

indicators.note: enters means the word for boy goes inside the name of the race

parts.note: the Palio is the famous bareback horse race around Siena's main square
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: An Italian architect's son takes part in Siena's famous horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The architect's 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea Palladio was the sixteenth-century Venetian designer whose villas inspired the Palladian style.

clue.text: Night wanderer revealed by hooter or sound of bell

explanation.surface: A nocturnal prowler gives himself away by his horn or a chime.
explanation.walkthrough: In Edward Lear's poem 'The Dong with a Luminous Nose', the creature wanders at night lit by its glowing nose; 'hooter' is slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear's nonsense creature roams by night with a shining nose; the second sense imitates the deep chime of a large bell.

clue.text: Standards I set in erratic novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of I and erratic are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone sets standards for an unpredictable book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but is the anagram signal; 'set in' just joins I to ERRATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are the principles or tests by which things are judged, i.e. benchmarks.

clue.text: Official report showing profit

explanation.surface: A formal statement reveals a company's earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: A tax return is an official report; a return on investment is a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A return is a formal statement filed with an authority, such as a tax form, and also the yield or gain on money invested.

clue.text: Some English kings and a French writer

parts.note: six English and British kings have been called George, so several are Georges
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list pairing several English monarchs with a French author.
explanation.walkthrough: Split differently, the kings' name plus 'and' gives the pen name of the novelist Aurore Dupin.
explanation.definitionFit: The nineteenth-century French novelist Aurore Dupin wrote under this male pen name.
